hook.convey: short lengths add up: many 100 m races (or about 20 m cricket pitches) end to end → a long distance; that long distance gets its own big unit, the kilometre; 1 km = 1000 m, and below the metre sits the cm, 1 m = 100 cm

use.hi: Cricket pitch lagbhag 20 m lamba hota hai. Aise 50 pitch ek line mein rakho, toh 50 × 20 = 1000 m ho jaate hain. Itni lambi doori ka apna ek bada unit hai: kilometre.
use.en: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. Put 50 such pitches in a line and 50 × 20 = 1000 m. A distance that long has its own big unit: the kilometre.

use.hi: School bus ghar se school tak kai km chalti hai. Aaj dekhenge ki 1 km mein kitne metre hote hain, aur 1 metre mein kitne cm.
use.en: The school bus goes several km from home to school. Today we see how many metres are in 1 km, and how many cm are in 1 metre.

explain.convey: 100 m sports-day race laid end to end again and again → at 1000 m the kilometre is complete → 1 km = 1000 m, not 100 m

point.hi: Sports day ki 100 m ki daud socho. Aisi daud ek ke baad ek jodte jao. Jab kul 1000 m ho jaate hain, tab 1 km poora hota hai. Toh 1 km = 1000 m, sirf 100 m nahi.
point.en: Think of the 100 m race on sports day. Join such races one after another. When the total reaches 1000 m, 1 km is complete. So 1 km = 1000 m, not just 100 m.

prompt.hi: 1 km poora karne ke liye 100 m wali kitni daud ek ke baad ek lagani padengi?
prompt.en: How many 100 m races, one after another, are needed to complete 1 km?

why.hi: ek daud 100 m ki hai, aur 10 × 100 m = 1000 m, jo 1 km hai
why.en: one race is 100 m, and 10 × 100 m = 1000 m, which is 1 km

simpler.hi: 100 m ki daud ek ke baad ek jodte jao. Jab kul 1000 m ho jaayein, tab 1 km poora hota hai.
simpler.en: Keep joining 100 m races one after another. When the total is 1000 m, 1 km is complete.

explain.convey: two separate facts, never mixed: 1 km = 1000 m (big to middle) and 1 m = 100 cm (middle to small); km biggest, then m, then cm

point.hi: Do alag jodiyan yaad rakho: 1 km = 1000 m, aur 1 m = 100 cm. Sabse bada unit km hai, phir m, aur sabse chhota cm. Metre ke andar 100 cm aate hain, 1000 nahi. Yeh rekha metre mein bani hai.
point.en: Remember two separate pairs: 1 km = 1000 m, and 1 m = 100 cm. The biggest unit is km, then m, and the smallest is cm. A metre holds 100 cm, not 1000. This line is marked in metres.

prompt.hi: Ek kapde ka tukda 2 m lamba hai. Woh kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: A piece of cloth is 2 m long. How many cm long is it?

why.hi: har m mein 100 cm hain, aur 2 × 100 = 200
why.en: each m holds 100 cm, and 2 × 100 = 200

simpler.hi: km aur m ki jodi mein 1000 hai, par m aur cm ki jodi mein 100. Ek metre mein 100 cm hote hain.
simpler.en: The km and m pair uses 1000, but the m and cm pair uses 100. One metre holds 100 cm.

explain.convey: the same distance in two units: 3 km = 3000 m → the bigger unit gives the smaller number, the smaller unit the bigger number, because one km holds 1000 m

point.hi: Ek hi doori ko km mein likho toh chhota number aata hai, metre mein likho toh bada number. Bada unit, chhota number, kyunki ek km mein bahut saare metre samaate hain. Yeh rekha metre mein hai.
point.en: Write the same distance in km and you get a smaller number; write it in metres and you get a bigger one. Bigger unit, smaller number, because one km holds many metres. This line is in metres.

prompt.hi: Ek sadak 8000 m lambi hai. Yeh sadak kitne km lambi hai?
prompt.en: A road is 8000 m long. How many km long is this road?

why.hi: har 1000 m ka 1 km banta hai, aur 8000 m mein 8 baar 1000 m hai
why.en: every 1000 m makes 1 km, and 8000 m is 8 lots of 1000 m

simpler.hi: Wahi doori km mein likho toh number chhota, metre mein likho toh bada. km bada unit hai, isliye usmein number chhota aata hai.
simpler.en: Write that distance in km and the number is small; in metres it is big. km is the bigger unit, so its number comes out smaller.

problem.hi: Park ke chaaron taraf ka raasta 250 m lamba hai. Rahul ko theek 1 km chalna hai. Rahul ko raaste ke kitne chakkar lagane honge?
problem.en: The path around a park is 250 m long. Rahul wants to walk exactly 1 km. How many rounds of the path must Rahul walk?

simpler.hi: 1 km mein 1000 m hote hain, aur ek chakkar 250 m ka hai. Gino, kitne 250 milkar 1000 bante hain.
simpler.en: 1 km has 1000 m, and one round is 250 m. Count how many 250s make 1000.

givens.hi: ek chakkar 250 m ka hai, aur Rahul ko 1 km chalna hai
givens.en: one round is 250 m, and Rahul must walk 1 km

simpler.en: The round is in metres, so write 1 km in metres too. 1 km = 1000 m.

do.en: Now add the distance of 2 rounds

why.hi: har chakkar 250 m ka hai
why.en: each round is 250 m

simpler.hi: Ek chakkar 250 m ka hai. Do chakkar matlab 250 + 250 = 500 m.
simpler.en: One round is 250 m. Two rounds means 250 + 250 = 500 m.

prompt.hi: 2 chakkar mein 500 m hue. Poore 1000 m ke liye kul kitne chakkar lagenge?

simpler.hi: 2 chakkar mein 500 m hote hain, aur 1000 m mein 500 do baar aata hai. Toh 2 chakkar wala hissa do baar lagega.
simpler.en: 2 rounds make 500 m, and 1000 m holds 500 twice. So the 2-round part is needed twice.

why.en: 2 rounds make 500 m, and 1000 m is twice that, so 4 rounds

answer.hi: Rahul ko raaste ke 4 chakkar lagane honge

say.en: Join the 100 m race 10 times, one after another: 10 × 100 = 1000 m. Only then is 1 km complete, not at 100 m.

point.en: Every km has 1000 m, so to change km to metres, multiply the number of km by 1000. Changing to the smaller unit, metres, makes the number bigger: smaller unit, bigger number. This line is marked in km.

point.hi: km aur m wali doori mein pehle km ko metre banao, phir bache metre jodo. Bache metre sau se kam hon, toh sau ki jagah 0 aata hai; use chhodna mat. Rekha par poore km pehle aate hain, phir bache metre.
point.en: In a distance in km and m, change the km to metres first, then add the metres left over. If the leftover metres are fewer than a hundred, a 0 goes in the hundreds place; don't drop it. On the line the whole km come first, then the metres left over.

explain.convey: m → km and m: 4500 m → take out the full thousands → 4000 m = 4 km, 500 m left → 4 km 500 m; changing to the bigger unit makes the number smaller

point.hi: Ulta bhi kar sakte hain. Har 1000 m = 1 km, toh metre mein jitne poore hazaar hain, utne km likho, aur jo metre bachein woh m mein. Board ki rekha par doori metre mein likhi hai.
point.en: We can go the other way too. Every 1000 m = 1 km, so write as many km as there are whole thousands in the metres, and the metres left over in m. The line on the board shows the distance in metres.

simpler.hi: km bada kadam hai, m chhota. Bade kadam kam lagte hain, isliye km mein number chhota hota hai.

hook.convey: every length has a unit that keeps its number easy to say: small things in cm, rooms, grounds and buildings in m, distances between places in km

explain.convey: benchmarks: 1 cm ≈ a fingernail's width → small things (pencil, book) in cm; 1 m ≈ one big stride → rooms and trees in m

1 m is about one big stride

point.hi: 1 cm lagbhag tumhare nakhoon ki chaudai hai, isliye pencil aur kitaab ko cm mein naapte hain. 1 m lagbhag ek lamba kadam hai, isliye kamra aur ped m mein naapte hain.
point.en: 1 cm is about the width of your fingernail, so we measure a pencil and a book in cm. 1 m is about one big stride, so we measure a room and a tree in m.

prompt.hi: Ek rubber ki lambai naapni hai. cm lenge ya m?

why.hi: rubber kuch nakhoon jitna hi lamba hai, ek lamba kadam bhi nahi
why.en: an eraser is only a few fingernails long, not even one big stride

simpler.hi: 1 centimetre lagbhag nakhoon ki chaudai hai, toh chhoti cheezein usmein naapte hain. 1 metre ek lamba kadam hai, toh kamra aur ped metre mein naapte hain.
simpler.en: 1 centimetre is about a fingernail wide, so small things are measured in it. 1 metre is about one big stride, so rooms and trees are measured in metres.

explain.convey: 1 m ≈ one big stride, 1 km ≈ a 12-minute walk → km is for distances between places; to choose a unit for a height, ask: a few strides, or many minutes of walking

mustSay.hi: km jagahon ki doori ke liye

point.hi: 1 m lagbhag ek lamba kadam hai, aur 1 km chalne mein lagbhag 12 minute lagte hain. Isliye km jagahon ki doori ke liye hai, jaise ghar se market. Kisi cheez ki oonchai ke liye socho: kuch kadam, ya bahut minute ki chaal.
point.en: 1 m is about one big stride, and walking 1 km takes about 12 minutes. So km is for distance between places, like home to the market. For the height of a thing, think: a few strides, or many minutes of walking.

prompt.hi: Ek mobile tower lagbhag 40 m ooncha hai. Tower ki oonchai 1 km se kam hai ya zyada?
prompt.en: A mobile tower is about 40 m tall. Is the tower's height less or more than 1 km?

why.hi: 40 m bas 40 kadam hain, jabki 1 km chalne mein 12 minute lagte hain; tower 1 km se bahut kam hai
why.en: 40 m is just 40 strides, while walking 1 km takes 12 minutes; the tower is far less than 1 km

simpler.hi: 1 metre lagbhag ek lamba kadam hai, aur 1 km chalne mein lagbhag 12 minute lagte hain. Oonchi cheez ke liye socho: kuch kadam, ya bahut minute ki chaal.
simpler.en: 1 metre is about one big stride, and walking 1 km takes about 12 minutes. For something tall, think: a few strides, or many minutes of walking.

problem.hi: Har cheez ke liye cm, m ya km chuno: school bag ki lambai, cricket pitch ki lambai, aur Jaipur se Delhi ki train yatra.
problem.en: Choose cm, m or km for each: the length of a school bag, the length of a cricket pitch, and the train journey from Jaipur to Delhi.

simpler.hi: Teen cheezein hain: bag, cricket pitch aur Jaipur se Delhi ka safar. Pehle socho har ek kitna lamba hai, phir unit chuno.
simpler.en: There are three things: a bag, a cricket pitch and the trip from Jaipur to Delhi. First think how long each one is, then choose the unit.

givens.hi: chunne ke liye unit: cm, m aur km
givens.en: units to choose from: cm, m and km

find.hi: teeno cheezon ke liye sahi unit
find.en: a suitable unit for all three

do.hi: School bag ki lambai ke liye unit chuno
do.en: Choose the unit for the length of the school bag

why.hi: bag 1 m se chhota hai, lagbhag 40 cm, ek lambe kadam se bhi kam
why.en: the bag is shorter than 1 m, about 40 cm, less than one big stride

simpler.hi: School bag ek lambe kadam se bhi chhota hai. Isliye uske liye cm theek hai.
simpler.en: A school bag is shorter than even one big stride. So cm is right for it.

do.hi: Cricket pitch ki lambai ke liye unit chuno
do.en: Choose the unit for the length of the cricket pitch

why.hi: pitch lagbhag 20 m ka hai, kuch lambe kadam, aur 1 km se bahut chhota
why.en: the pitch is about 20 m, a few big strides, far less than 1 km

simpler.hi: Cricket pitch kuch lambe kadmon jitni hai, aur ek km se bahut chhoti. Isliye uske liye m theek hai.
simpler.en: A cricket pitch is a few big strides long, and far less than one km. So m is right for it.

prompt.hi: Ab Jaipur se Delhi ki train yatra ke liye unit chuno: cm, m ya km?
prompt.en: Now choose the unit for the train journey from Jaipur to Delhi: cm, m or km?

simpler.hi: Jaipur se Delhi bahut door hai, wahan tak chalne mein kai din lag jaayenge. Jagahon ki doori ke liye sabse bada unit lete hain.
simpler.en: Jaipur to Delhi is very far; walking there would take days. For distances between places we use the biggest unit.

why.hi: school bag cm mein aur cricket pitch m mein naapte hain, par Jaipur se Delhi ki doori km mein
why.en: a school bag is measured in cm and a cricket pitch in m, but Jaipur to Delhi in km

answer.hi: school bag cm mein, cricket pitch m mein, aur Jaipur se Delhi ki yatra km mein
answer.en: the school bag in cm, the cricket pitch in m, and the Jaipur to Delhi journey in km

why.hi: chhoti cheezein cm mein, kamre aur maidan m mein, aur do jagahon ke beech ki doori km mein naapte hain
why.en: small things are measured in cm, rooms and grounds in m, and distances between two places in km

prompt.hi: Ek bada aam ka ped lagbhag 15 m ooncha hai. Agar woh gir kar zameen par pada ho aur tum uske saath-saath chalo, toh kuch second lagenge ya kai minute?
prompt.en: A big mango tree is about 15 m tall. If it had fallen and lay on the ground and you walked along it, would it take a few seconds or many minutes?

why.hi: 15 m bas 15 lambe kadam hain, kuch second ki chaal; kai minute toh km jitni doori mein lagte hain
why.en: 15 m is just 15 long strides, a few seconds' walk; many minutes is for a km-long distance

simpler.hi: Ek metre lagbhag ek lamba kadam hai. Socho, 15 kadam chalne mein kitna samay lagta hai.
simpler.en: A metre is about one long stride. Think how long it takes to walk 15 strides.

prompt.hi: School ke playground ke board par lambai '90' likhi hai, par unit mit gaya hai. {friendF} kehti hai ki yeh 90 m hogi. Kya yeh andaaza theek hai?
prompt.en: The school playground's sign gives its length as '90', but the unit has rubbed off. {friendF} says it must be 90 m. Is that a sensible guess?

why.hi: 90 m matlab lagbhag 90 lambe kadam, ek playground jitna; 90 km toh ghanton ki chaal hai
why.en: 90 m is about 90 long strides, playground-sized; 90 km would be hours of walking

simpler.hi: 90 m ka matlab lagbhag 90 lambe kadam. Socho, playground ek sire se doosre tak itna lamba lagta hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: 90 m means about 90 long strides. Think whether a playground feels that long from end to end.

ladder.why: three objects, three units: pencil cm, door m, Delhi to Agra km
a tall building is still m, not km: 10 storeys is about 30 m
a distance between cities → km, with the reason why

remediation.move: benchmark ladder: 1 m = one big stride, 1 km = about a 12-minute walk → the child sizes the thing in strides before choosing

say.hi: Ek lamba kadam lagbhag 1 m hota hai, aur 12 minute ki chaal lagbhag 1 km. Kuch bhi bada lage, pehle socho ki woh kitne kadam ka hai.
say.en: One big stride is about 1 m, and a 12-minute walk is about 1 km. However big something looks, first think how many strides it is.

simpler.hi: 1 m lagbhag ek lamba kadam hai. 1 km chalne mein lagbhag 12 minute lagte hain.
simpler.en: 1 m is about one big stride. Walking 1 km takes about 12 minutes.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne likha: bijli ka khamba lagbhag 9 km ooncha hai. Kya km sahi unit hai? Agar nahi, toh kaunsa?
prompt.en: {friend} wrote: an electric pole is about 9 km tall. Is km the right unit? If not, which one is?

why.hi: 9 m lagbhag 9 lambe kadam hain, khambe jitna; 9 nakhoon bahut chhote aur 9 km bahut bada
why.en: 9 m is about 9 long strides, pole-sized; 9 fingernails is far too small and 9 km far too big

simpler.hi: 9 lambe kadam ek bijli ke khambe jitne oonche lagte hain. 9 nakhoon bahut chhote hain, aur 9 km bahut bade.
simpler.en: 9 big strides is about as tall as an electric pole. 9 fingernails is far too small, and 9 km far too big.
